2609.24877.title: Decomposing Error and Style in Automated Clinical Coding
2609.24877.paper_summary: In automated clinical coding, where the label space spans tens of thousands of diagnosis and procedure codes, models are currently evaluated against a single gold annotation, treating any deviation as error. But we find when two teams code the same 110 ACI-Bench encounters, they agree on only 73% of codes (Jaccard similarity) for the same note; even after an independent clinical audit removes erroneous codes, agreement rises only to 77%. Is that gap error or something systematic? We model the systematic component as coding style $ψ$, a coder- or site-specific policy over what to code and how much to document, and recast coding as $p(\mathrm{code}\mid\mathrm{note},ψ)$, estimating $ψ$ with a 10-dimension rubric. If style were noise, conditioning on it would do nothing. Instead, across five datasets a model conditioned with a data-matching style raises ICD F1 by up to 26 points and an extreme mismatched one lowers it by up to 21. Four prompt based coding methods spanning 39-49 F1 converge to 52-56 once style is supplied (All p<0.05). Much of what single-gold evaluation charges to model error is recoverable, unmodeled style.
2609.24877.paper_summary_zh: 在自動化臨床編碼中，標籤空間涵蓋數萬個診斷和程序代碼，當前模型是根據單一的金標註進行評估，將任何偏差視為錯誤。<lb/>但我們發現，當兩個團隊對同一 110 個 ACI-Bench 事件進行編碼時，他們對同一筆記的代碼僅有 73% 的一致性（Jaccard 相似度）；即使在獨立的臨床審核去除錯誤代碼後，一致性也僅上升至 77%。<lb/>這個差距是錯誤還是某種系統性問題？<lb/>我們將系統性成分建模為編碼風格 $ψ$，這是一種針對編碼內容和文檔量的編碼者或地點特定政策，並將編碼重新表述為 $p(\mathrm{code}\mid\mathrm{note},ψ)$，用一個 10 維的評分標準來估計 $ψ$。<lb/>如果風格只是噪音，對其進行條件化將沒有任何作用。<lb/>相反，在五個數據集上，使用數據匹配風格進行條件化的模型使 ICD F1 提升了最多 26 分，而極端不匹配的風格則使其降低了最多 21 分。<lb/>四種基於提示的編碼方法，F1 分數範圍為 39-49，一旦提供風格，便會收斂至 52-56（所有 p<0.05）。<lb/>許多單一金標註評估所指責的模型錯誤是可恢復的，未建模的風格。
